thread:
ana: quick thought exercise: what if we make gold sets a CAS-backed manifest + small index instead of monolithic blobs? pros/cons?

ryan: + dedupe across teams, chunk-level caching in CI, smaller updates (only changed samples). - more complex client logic.

joan: concerned about partial pulls for offline dev. need a manifest-first workflow: manifest (ids + tokenizer-id) is tiny and can be checked into repo; payloads fetched on demand.

lee: agreed. cli sketch: `ri gold fetch --manifest MANIFEST --only-missing` where manifest lists sha256s and tokenizer variant. CI runners cache chunks by sha.

gold-bot: stat: 70% of gold bytes overlap between top-50 sets. CAS could cut storage and bandwidth a lot.

ryan: promotion flow: shadow overrides map to their own shadow-id that references same chunks; promotion creates new canonical_id pointing to existing manifest. telemetry emits canonical_id + optional shadow_id.

joan: need canonicalization rules in manifest: store raw_input, normalized_tokens (per tokenizer-id) and expected_output_hash. diff tooling uses normalized_tokens to avoid FP due to tokenization drift.

ci-bot: runner note: bake top-N chunk cache into images and provide a signed-url proxy with short TTLs. reduces flakiness.

ana: actionables: ryan to prototype manifest proto (schema + client) this week; lee to sketch CLI commands; joan to write a short note on normalization rules. we'll test with top-10 golds first.

ana: one-liner decision: lean CAS+manifest (manifest in-repo, chunks in catalog) + shadowing semantics. we'll validate after proto. :thumbsup:
